intent: Test arch_cpu.sh to 100% line coverage and take it off the shell coverage allowlist, clearing the second of the eight untested fixes/lib libraries.
scope: Non-goal: arch_sysctl.sh's measurement problem, which this commit deliberately leaves untouched
changes: Added CPU_SYSFS_ROOT, BLOCK_SYSFS_ROOT, UDEV_RULES_DIR and CPUPOWER_CONF_FILE overrides to arch_cpu.sh, each defaulting to the real path so production behaviour is unchanged
Added _t_make_cpu, _t_make_block, _t_sched and _t_udev to arch_desktop_harness.sh so a case can present hardware this host does not have, such as a rotational disk
Added test_arch_cpu.sh: 28 assertions over 14 cases covering both functions, including the mixed-governor case, all three I/O scheduler targets, and the already-configured cpupower path
Removed arch_cpu.sh from meta/shell-coverage-allowlist.txt, taking it from 91 to 90 entries

verification.evidence: arch_cpu.sh: 57/57 lines = 100.00%, exit 0, so a shortfall would have been a non-zero exit.

verification.command: bash meta/scripts/check_shell_coverage.sh .../fixes/lib/arch_cpu.sh (after removing the allowlist line)
verification.evidence: check_shell_coverage.sh: every checked shell library meets the coverage bar
All fixes lib test files passed; arch_cpu: 28 passed, 0 failed.

risks: A test asserting cpupower is absent initially passed for the wrong reason: _t_hide keeps $FAKE_BIN on PATH, so the harness's own default stub still satisfied has_cmd. Fixed by unstubbing before hiding, and the assertion now fails if that ordering is lost.
The measurement of arch_cpu.sh through the same harness that arch_sysctl.sh uses shows the harness is not the cause of arch_sysctl.sh's unmeasurability
rollback: git revert the commit, then re-add the arch_cpu.sh line to meta/shell-coverage-allowlist.txt
Re-run check_shell_coverage.sh to confirm the gate passes again with the exemption restored
